description.narrative:
The Global Fund for Coral Reefs (GFCR) was launched in 2020, and is a blended financing mechanism, The fund's objective is to enhance the resilience of costal reef ecosystems, communities and economies by unlocking new public and private resources. The GFCR’s resilience-focused portfolio deploys catalytic grants and investments to implement market-based solutions that address the causes of ecosystem stress and degradation across 20+ developing nations. By 2025 the following Coral Nations have been supported: The Bahamas, Belize, Brazil, Colombia, Egypt, Fiji, Guatemala, Honduras, Indonesia, Jordan, Kenya, Maldives, Marshall Islands, Mexico, Micronesia, Mozambique, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Sri Lanka andTanzania.
The GFCR Coalition comprised more than 60 members spanning supported coral nations, donor governments, philanthropies, investment partners, conservation organizations, and strategic alliances.
